ἁμαρτίας λέγεσθαι νομιστέον· οὗτος γὰρ κατὰ τὴν προτέραν ἀναστροφὴν καὶ τὰς
ἐπιθυμίας τῆς ἀπάτης, διὰ τοῦ ἁμαρτάνειν καὶ μηδέποτε ἀφθαρσίας τι ποιεῖν ἀλλ'
ὅλα τὰ τῆς φθορᾶς ἐργάζεσθαι, ἀεὶ φθείρεται. αἱ μὲν οὖν ἐπιθυμίαι τῆς ἀπάτης καὶ ἡ
προτέρα ἀναστροφὴ ἐνεργοῦσι τὸ φθείρεσθαι αὐτόν, καὶ οὐδέπω πάντῃ ἔφθαρται
ὅσον ταῦτα ποιεῖ, ἀλλὰ φθείρεται· ὁ δὲ λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ οὐ φθείρει ἀλλὰ ἀποκτένει
τὸν παλαιὸν ἄνθρωπον ἐπὶ τῷ ζωοποιῆσαι, ἐγὼ γάρ, φησίν, ἀποκτένω καὶ ζῇν
ποιή ω, καὶ ὅταν ἀπέκτενεν αὐτοὺ τότε ἐξεζήτουν αὐτόν. ἔτι ζητήσεις πῶς ὁ κατὰ
τὴν κακίαν πεπαλαιωμένος παλαιὸς ἄνθρωπος λέγεται. καὶ μήποτε ὥσπερ ἀνακαινοῖ
καὶ ἀνακτίζει ἡ ἀρετή, οὕτως ἡ ἐναντία αὐτῇ κακία παλαιοῖ, ὡς καὶ τῆς παλαιότητος
σημεῖα γίνεσθαι περὶ τὴν ψυχὴν οἱονεὶ τὰς ῥυτίδας, ὥσπερ γίνεται ἐπὶ τῶν
γηρασκόντων σωμάτων. διὰ τοῦτο ἔνδοξον αὐτῷ παρί τη ι τὴν ἐκκλη ίαν Χριστός,
μὴ ἔχου αν πίλον ἢ ῥυτίδα ἤ τι τῶν τοιούτων· ὅσον μὲν γὰρ ἔχει σημεῖα τῆς
παλαιότητος, ἔχει καὶ τὴν ῥυτίδα· ὅταν δὲ ἀπόθηται τὸν παλαιὸν ἄνθρωπον, ἅπαντα
ἀκμάζει καὶ πᾶσα ῥυτὶς ἐξαφανίζεται. ἀπάτης δέ ἐστιν ἐπιθυμία ἡ μοχθηρὰ ἐπιθυμία
καὶ ἡ φαύλη. [ iv 23] ἀνανεοῦσθε δὲ τῷ πνεύματι τοῦ νοὸς ὑμῶν. εἰ χρὴ ἀνανεοῦσθαι
κατὰ τὴν λέξιν ταύτην οὔτε ἁπλῶς ἐν τῷ πνεύματι οὔτε ἐν τῷ νοΐ, ἀλλ' ἐν τῷ
πνεύματι τοῦ νοὸς ὑμῶν, ζητητέον ἰδίᾳ τίς ὁ νοῦς ἡμῶν καὶ τί τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ.
πρόσχες δὲ καὶ τῷ ψαλῶ τῷ πνεύματι ψαλῶ δὲ καὶ τῷ νοΐ, προ εύξομαι τῷ πνεύματι
προ εύξομαι καὶ τῷ νοΐ. ἐπιστήσεις οὖν εἰ, ὥσπερ ἔστι πολλὰ πνεύματα καὶ ἕκαστόν
τινι ᾠκείωται, οὕτως ἔστιν τι πνεῦμα ᾠκειωμένον ἡμῶν τῷ νοΐ, ὅπερ τοῦ νοὸς ἡμῶν
ἀποκαθαιρομένου καὶ πᾶσαν ἀποβαλόντος ἀχλὺν ᾠκειωμένον αὐτῷ ἀνανεοῖ ἡμᾶς. [
iv 24a. καὶ ἐνδύσασθε τὸν καινὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν κατὰ Θεὸν κτισθέντα.] εἰ θέλομεν
ἐνδύσασθαι τὸν καινὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν κατὰ Θεὸν κτισθέντα, νοήσωμεν τὸ μιμηταί
μου γίνε θε καθὼ κἀγὼ Χρι τοῦ καὶ τὸ ζῶ δὲ οὐκέτι ἐγὼ ζῇ δὲ ἐν ἐμοὶ Χρι τό · καὶ
ἁπαξαπλῶς μορφωθέντα τὸν Χρι τὸν ἐν ἡμῖν ὅλον καὶ κατὰ πᾶσαν πρᾶξιν δείξομεν.
[ iv 25a] διὸ ἀποθέμενοι τὸ ψεῦδος λαλεῖτε ἀλήθειαν ἕκαστος μετὰ τοῦ πλησίον
αὐτοῦ. οἱ μὲν ἁπλούστεροι πλέον τοῦ ἠθικοῦ οὐδὲν οἰήσονται λέγεσθαι ἐκ τοῦ
λεγομένου· ἡμεῖς δέ, ἐναντίον εἶναι πειθόμενοι τῇ ἀληθείᾳ τὸ ψεῦδος, τὸ ἐναντίον
τῇ καθηκόντως λαλουμένῃ ἀληθείᾳ πρὸς μόνον τὸν πλησίον ζητοῦμεν ψεῦδος
ἀποθέσθαι ὅπερ ἐστὶν ἡ ψευδοδοξία (ἔργον δὲ οὐ τὸ τυχόν ἐστι πρὸς τ<ῷ> ἀποθέσθαι
ἐκεῖνο τὸ ψεῦδος καὶ τὸ οὕτως ψεῦδος ἀποθέσθαι, καὶ γὰρ δόκιμον δεῖ εἶναι
τραπεζίτην καὶ πάντα δοκιμάζειν ἱκανόν, ἵνα μόνον κατέχωμεν τὸ καλὸν ἀπὸ δὲ
παντὸ εἴδου πονηροῦ ἀπεχώμεθα)· ἐναντίον δὲ τῷ κατὰ τὰς ψευδοδοξίας ψεύδει
ἐστὶν ἡ σωτήριος ἀλήθεια. τὸ δὲ λαλεῖτε ἀλήθειαν ἕκαστος μετὰ τοῦ πλησίον αὐτοῦ
εἴληπται ἀπὸ τοῦ Ζαχαρίου. [ iv 26a] ὀργίζεσθε καὶ μὴ ἁμαρτάνετε. ὅτι ἀπὸ τοῦ
τετάρτου ψαλμοῦ τοῦτο εἴληπται δῆλόν ἐστιν. δύο δὲ σημαίνεται ἐκ τῆς ὀργίζεσθαι
φωνῆς· ἢ τὸ ἀπροαίρετον, ὅπερ τινὲς ἐκάλεσαν προ<σ>πάθειαν, ἥτις συμβήσεται καὶ
τοῖς τελείοις ἀπροαίρετόν τι πάσχουσι κατὰ τὰ τοιάδε εἰς ὀργὴν προκαλούμενα
συμπτώματα· ἕτερον δέ, ὅταν ἤδη ἡ συγκατάθεσις παραδέχηται τὸ καθήκειν
τιμωρεῖσθαι τὸν ἠδικη <κ>έν<αι> νομιζόμενον, ὅπερ ὡς ἐφ' ἡμῖν τυγχάνον κελεύει
ἀποθέσθαι ὁ ἀπό στολος ἡμᾶς. τὸ πρότερον οὖν τῶν σημαινομένων δηλοῦται ἐν τῷ
ὀργίζεσθε καὶ μὴ ἁμαρτάνετε ἀντὶ τοῦ «εἰ καὶ παρεδέξασθέ ποτε τὴν ὀργήν, ἀλλὰ
ἄπρακτον καταλείψατε.» [ iv 26b] ὁ ἥλιος μὴ ἐπιδυέτω ἐπὶ τῷ παροργισμῷ ὑμῶν. ἐὰν
τὸν αἰσθητὸν ἥλιον ἀκούσωμεν λέγεσθαι, ἁμαρτησόμεθα ὅτε ὀργιζόμεθα καὶ
τηροῦμεν τὴν ὀργὴν τοῦ ἡλίου δύνοντος, ὅπερ ἄτοπον εἶναι νομίζω. μήποτ' οὖν ὁ
ἀληθινὸς ἥλιος, ὥσπερ δύσεται ἐπὶ τοὺς πονηροὺς προφήτας κατὰ τὸ εἰρημένον
pass_a_gloss: [the old man made old by] sin must be thought to be what is said. For this man, according to the earlier way of life and the desires of the deceit, by sinning and never doing anything of incorruption but working all the things of corruption, is always being corrupted. Therefore the desires of the deceit and the earlier way of life work his being corrupted, and he has not yet in every way been corrupted as long as he does these things, but he is being corrupted. But the Word of God does not corrupt but kills the old man for the purpose of making alive: for I, he says, will kill and make to live; and when he killed them, then they sought him out. Still you will seek how the old man who has been made old according to wickedness is so called. And perhaps, as virtue renews and re-creates, so the wickedness contrary to it makes old, so that signs of oldness come to be about the soul, like wrinkles, as happens on bodies growing old. Because of this Christ presents the church to himself glorious, not having spot or wrinkle or any of such things; for as much as it has signs of oldness, it has also the wrinkle; but when it puts off the old man, all things are at their peak and every wrinkle is made to disappear. Desire of deceit is the wicked desire and the base one. [4:23] Be renewed in the spirit of your mind. If it is necessary to be renewed, according to this phrase, neither simply in the spirit nor in the mind, but in the spirit of your mind, one must inquire separately what our mind is and what its spirit is. Pay attention also to: I will sing with the spirit, I will sing also with the mind; I will pray with the spirit, I will pray also with the mind. You will consider then whether, just as there are many spirits and each has been made proper to someone, so there is some spirit made proper to our mind, which, our mind being cleansed and having thrown off all mist, being proper to it, renews us. [4:24a] And put on the new man created according to God. If we wish to put on the new man created according to God, let us understand the be imitators of me as I also of Christ, and the I live no longer I, but Christ lives in me; and in sum we will show Christ formed in us whole and according to every action. [4:25a] Wherefore having put off the lie speak truth each with his neighbor. The simpler ones will suppose nothing more than the ethical is said from what is said; but we, being persuaded that the lie is contrary to the truth, seek to put off the lie contrary to the truth fittingly spoken to the neighbor only, which is false opinion (it is no chance work to put off that lie and to put off lie in this way, for one must be an approved banker and able to test all things, so that we hold only the good and keep away from every form of evil); and contrary to the lie according to false opinions is the saving truth. The speak truth each with his neighbor has been taken from Zechariah. [4:26a] Be angry and do not sin. That this has been taken from the fourth psalm is clear. Two things are signified by the word be angry: either the unchosen, which some called pre-passion, which will happen also to the perfect who suffer something unchosen in such incidents calling to anger; and another, when already the assent admits that it is fitting to punish the one thought to have done wrong, which, as being in our power, the apostle orders us to put off. Therefore the first of the meanings is shown in be angry and do not sin, instead of: even if you once admitted the anger, yet leave it inactive. [4:26b] Let the sun not set upon your provocation. If we hear the sensible sun spoken of, we will sin when we are angry and keep the anger while the sun is setting, which I think is absurd. Perhaps then the true sun, as it will set upon the wicked prophets according to what was said
pass_b_english: sin is to be understood as meant. For by his former way of life and the desires of deceit, through sinning and never doing anything that belongs to incorruption but working everything that belongs to corruption, this man is always being corrupted. So the desires of deceit and the former way of life bring about his corruption; and as long as he does these things he has not yet been wholly corrupted, but he is being corrupted. The Word of God, however, does not corrupt: he kills the old man in order to make him alive. “For I kill,” he says, “and I make alive” (Deuteronomy 32:39); and “when he killed them, then they sought him” (Psalm 78:34).

You will ask further how the old man is the one grown old in wickedness. Perhaps, just as virtue renews and creates afresh, so wickedness, its opposite, makes old, so that signs of age, wrinkles as it were, appear on the soul, as they do on bodies growing old. That is why Christ presents the church to himself glorious, “not having spot or wrinkle or any such thing” (Ephesians 5:27). For as long as one bears the signs of age, one has the wrinkle too; but when one puts off the old man, everything is in its prime and every wrinkle vanishes. And the desire of deceit is wicked and base desire.

“And be renewed in the spirit of your mind” (Ephesians 4:23). If, by this wording, we must be renewed neither simply in the spirit nor in the mind, but in the spirit of our mind, we must ask on its own what our mind is and what its spirit is. Notice also the words “I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing with the mind also; I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray with the mind also” (1 Corinthians 14:15). Consider, then, whether, just as there are many spirits and each belongs closely to someone, so there is a spirit that belongs to our mind; and when our mind is being cleansed and has thrown off all its mist, this spirit, being its own, renews us.

“And put on the new man, created according to God” (Ephesians 4:24). If we want to put on the new man created according to God, let us take to heart “Be imitators of me, as I also am of Christ” (1 Corinthians 11:1), and “I live, yet no longer I, but Christ lives in me” (Galatians 2:20). In a word, we will show Christ formed in us, whole, and in every action.

“Therefore, putting away the lie, speak truth each one with his neighbor” (Ephesians 4:25). Simpler readers will think that nothing more than a moral rule is said here. But we are persuaded that the lie is the opposite of the truth, and so the lie we seek to put away, the one opposed to the truth that is fittingly spoken to the neighbor alone, is false belief. It is no ordinary task to put away that lie, and to put away a lie of this kind; for one must be an approved money-changer, able to test everything, so that we hold fast only to what is good and keep away from every form of evil (1 Thessalonians 5:21–22). And what stands against the lie that lies in false beliefs is saving truth. The words “speak truth each one with his neighbor” are taken from Zechariah (Zechariah 8:16).

“Be angry and do not sin” (Ephesians 4:26). It is clear that this is taken from the fourth Psalm (Psalm 4:4). The word “be angry” signifies two things. One is the involuntary, which some have called a pre-passion; it will happen even to the perfect, who suffer something involuntary when circumstances of this kind provoke them to anger. The other is when assent already accepts that it is fitting to punish the one thought to have done wrong; and this, since it lies in our power, the apostle commands us to put away. So it is the first of these meanings that is shown in “Be angry and do not sin,” in place of “even if you have at some time admitted anger, leave it without effect.”

“Do not let the sun go down on your provocation” (Ephesians 4:26). If we take this as said of the sun we see, then we will sin when we are angry and keep our anger while the sun goes down, which I think is absurd. choices.english: sin is to be understood as meant
choices.why: The section opens mid-sentence; u04-rem-close ends “the old man … made old by the”. The fragment is kept as a continuation, not rewritten as a full sentence.

choices.english: since it lies in our power
choices.why: Origen’s point is that the second kind of anger is voluntary; the old English kept this, but dropped “the perfect” suffer the first kind involuntarily.

choices.english: If we take this as said of the sun we see
choices.why: No “only” is in the Greek; the old English added it.

choices.english: fittingly spoken to the neighbor alone
choices.why: Kept literal; the sense of μόνον is not clear, so no interpretation is added.

choices.english: Deuteronomy 32:39; Psalm 78:34; Ephesians 5:27; 1 Corinthians 14:15; 11:1; Galatians 2:20; 1 Thessalonians 5:21–22; Zechariah 8:16; Psalm 4:4
choices.why: Each checked against the KJV text of the verse; Psalm 77:34 LXX = Psalm 78:34 English.
